source.title: IMPROVING THE ADAPTIVE MOMENT ESTIMATION OPTIMIZATION METHODS FOR MODERN MACHINE LEARNING

record.tranche_reason: Compares validation accuracy across optimizers on several image classification and segmentation tasks, using a different set of models and measures than the claim's cited optimizer studies.
record.gate_note: Optimizer comparison results are reported in Tables 4.1–4.4; the thesis does not report results on random-label fitting, width sweeps, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. The figure-only multi-layer CIFAR-10 comparison is not extracted because the values cannot be assigned reliably from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Tables 4.1–4.3 report held-out accuracy for existing adaptive optimizers versus SGD on MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks. These comparisons bear on V4 in additional settings, although the tuning protocol and relative training performance are unspecified.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the author concludes that ADAM Plus improves convergence and average accuracy over the tested optimizers. The conclusion also acknowledges a trade-off between fast and precise convergence; the thesis does not establish a controlled generalization advantage at matched training performance.
record.recipe_differences: Compares validation accuracy for common optimizers on image tasks, but centers on the proposed ADAM Plus method; training accuracy, optimizer tuning, and whether training performance was equal are not reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported validation accuracy comparisons vary by dataset and architecture; the U-net comparison does not include SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: ADAM Plus achieves validation accuracies of 0.9864, 0.9853 and 0.6886 in the three classification tables.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed ADAM Plus optimizer improves validation accuracy over the tested optimizer baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: U-net validation accuracies are 0.9698 for Adam, 0.9725 for Nadam and 0.9736 for ADAM Plus; no SGD result is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizer choice affects U-net segmentation validation accuracy under the tested recipe.

record.problems: The thesis does not report uncertainty, optimizer tuning details, or corresponding training performance for the tabulated validation accuracies. The U-net table omits SGD, and the multi-layer CIFAR-10 comparison is figure-only in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The multi-layer Cifar10 optimizer comparison at epoch 5 and batch size 50 is shown in Figure 4.13, but the supplied text gives no numerical values and does not support assigning the plotted values to individual optimizers.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Specified limited versus broader tuning; matched training performance or convergence; language benchmarks; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations of the training recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with other generalization measures.

record.verdict_notes: This thesis is not an original source for V4. Its reversed comparisons qualify an 'often' claim rather than refute it universally. No uncertainty or optimizer-search protocol is reported. Training curves exist for ADAM Plus, but do not establish matched training performance across optimizers. Figure 4.13 is already declared in rows_left_out, and its optimizer-specific values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons
language benchmarks, training performance comparisons, limited versus broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD
